messages:
Samir P.: Anyone else seeing a latency spike in asia-east1? Generator p95 jumped from ~120ms to 900ms and a bunch of 502s started showing up around 03:03 UTC.
Infra Alert Bot: [ALERT] Instance evictions detected in asia-east1 (preemptible). 28 nodes marked TERMINATED in last 5m. Link: https://monitoring.redwood/alerts/evictions-asia1 :rotating_light:
Olivia Chen: yup seeing it. Autoscaler triggered but nodes didn't come up fast enough. Preemptible pool lost ~70% of capacity.
Maria Gomez: confirmed from GCE events. Quietly high eviction rate for the pool "inference-spot-asia1". Looks like it was a scheduling churn in that AZ.
Kai Nakamura: grabbing node list now.
Kai Nakamura: `kubectl get nodes -l pool=spot-asia1 -o wide` shows a lot NotReady/Shutdown. Also kube-proxy flapping on some nodes.
Samir P.: can we flip traffic to on-demand pools in the asia endpoint routing? want to avoid cross-region fanout if possible.
Lex (oncall): I'm on it. Starting with routing fallback to dedi-asia1 and then to us-west1 if needed.
Olivia Chen: +1. Also suggest temporarily pinning model to a quantized variant that needs fewer GPUs for cost while we recover.
Maria Gomez: I'll disable scale-to-zero for the on-demand pool so nodes come up faster. Running:
```
kubectl patch configmap autoscaler-config -n infra --type merge -p '{"data":{"scale_to_zero":"false"}}'
```
Kai Nakamura: queued a resize for dhe-dedi-asia1: `gcloud compute instance-groups managed resize dedi-asia1 --size=8`
Infra Alert Bot: [INFO] Routing policy applied: region-fallback -> dedi-asia1 (priority 1), us-west1 (priority 2).
Samir P.: can we whitelist critical routes only for dedi for now? we don't want batch jobs to soak the dedi pool.
Lex (oncall): done — updated route weights, critical routes only.
Olivia Chen: after routing flip p95 went down to ~220ms but some errors still trickling. Looks like a small subset of requests still hitting the disrupted nodes (sticky sessions maybe).
Kai Nakamura: killing the old spot node kubelets to force pods to reschedule:
```
for n in $(kubectl get nodes -l pool=spot-asia1 -o name); do kubectl drain $n --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force; done
```
This freed pods to be scheduled on dedi nodes.
Maria Gomez: nodes drained and many pods rescheduled. Pod restarts ~1.2k across inference namespace.
Samir P.: thanks. any idea root cause? single AZ or fleet-wide?
Maria Gomez: eviction logs point to a maintenance event in asia-east1-a then rippled to asia-east1-b due to autoscaler placement compaction. Seems cloud preempt too.
Olivia Chen: we should consider adding a safety buffer to spot pools or set a lower minimum for critical deployments. Current min was 0 which made us vulnerable.
Lex (oncall): agreed. For now I raised spot pool min to 3 and increased target for dedi pool to keep p95 stable.
Kai Nakamura: monitoring shows error rate back to normal band. p95 ~140ms and success rate ~99.7%.
Infra Alert Bot: [RESOLVED] Eviction alert cleared for asia-east1. 5m sustained normal node counts.
Samir P.: awesome. Maria please open a follow-up ticket to investigate AZ churn and talk to cloud provider — include eviction timestamps and node metadata. Put cost-impact estimate too.
Maria Gomez: will do. Estimated extra on-demand spend for recovery ~ $2.8k over the event window. Adding to ticket.
Olivia Chen: action items: add buffer config to spot pool templates, add sticky-session eviction mitigation (prefer session-less routing or faster failover), and add runbook step to disable scale-to-zero on dedi during regional instability.
Lex (oncall): adding runbook edits now. Will also schedule postmortem sync tomorrow 09:30 PT.
Kai Nakamura: one more note — the autoscaler probe timeout was default 10s, increasing to 30s helped avoid marking nodes NotReady during transient network blips. I'll include that in the PR.
Samir P.: thanks everyone. summary: preemptible evictions in asia-east1 caused partial outage -> routing fallback to on-demand + forced drains -> pods rescheduled -> restored. Follow-ups and cost ticket assigned. :white_check_mark:
